text:
linus: Heads-up — seit ~03:10 i've been seeing p99 spikes (+30-50ms) from dedicated-pool-usw1 for small chat workloads. Looks like one tenant is saturating TOR egress and the pool scheduler is fragmenting. anyone else?
aj: saw the alert. can you paste the quick logs? which rack?
linus: rack r12 and r13. short log dump: 
```
2026-02-18T03:12:07Z shard-proxy[proxy-7]: egress_bytes tenant=tn-42 delta=120MB/s iface=tor-eth1 burst=true
2026-02-18T03:12:09Z allocator[alloc-5]: slice-alloc tenant=tn-43->dedicated-pool-usw1 slot=12 prefill=true
2026-02-18T03:12:10Z scheduler[sch]: soft-shed tenant=tn-88 reason=egress-spillback
```
linus: interestingly the tenant doing the heavy egress is pinned to a fractional slice in the same dedicated pool — the scheduler is trying to give them prefills and it's creating extra cross-attach traffic.
priya: is this the fallback routing we recently rolled? iirc we changed routing policy to spill prefill across racks when warm pool pressure hits threshold. could be we're now blowing intra-rack TOR link.
maria: FYI billing flagged a one-hour egress blip for that org — ~$1.6k unexpected. ops is asking for mitigation now.
oncall-sre: i'm oncall — quick mitigation: can we leash per-tenant egress at the pool-proxy level to 40MB/s and throttle prefill concurrency? that should stop immediate spill.
ops-automation: we can toggle per-tenant egress leash via the feature flag `egress_leash_per_tenant` in prod-config, path: /configs/pool-proxy/egress.json. patch command: 
```bash
rctl config set prod pool-proxy egress_leash_per_tenant=true
rctl config set prod pool-proxy egress_leash_bytes_per_sec=41943040
```
ops-automation: also: throttling prefill concurrency: 
```bash
rctl config set prod allocator prefill_concurrency_limit=2
```
aj: before we flip anything, can we confirm tenant tn-42 is the cause? run a quick query: 
```sql
SELECT tenant, sum(egress_bytes) as bytes FROM net.tor_stats WHERE time > now() - 10m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 5;
```
linus: ran it, tn-42 and tn-99 top the list. tn-42 is the one doing lots of small write-ish traffic (logging/kv-backups), tn-99 is a noisy prefill job. tn-99 has been recently promoted to dedicated-fractional.
priya: i think the scheduler fallback policy mis-classified prefill jobs as latency-sensitive; it accelerated their warmup and caused duplicate prefetches across racks. i'll open a tiny PR to make prefill jobs lower priority for cross-rack warmup.
maria: short-term — please flip the egress_leash flag and lower prefill_concurrency. ops will reconcile billing after.
oncall-sre: doing it now. tagging @aj @linus for verification. :party_parrot:
devops-bot: config change recorded: user=oncall-sre action=set egress_leash_per_tenant=true at=2026-02-18T03:17:12Z
ops-automation: egress leash applied, limit=40MB/s for tenants in dedicated-pool-usw1. prefill_concurrency=2 applied.
aj: can you watch p99 and egress bytes for 10m?
linus: monitoring — p99 dropping from 220ms to ~110ms within 90s. egress bytes for tn-99 dropped to ~8MB/s.
priya: opening PR referencing the fallback routing policy: reduce cross-rack prefill priority and add an isolation check that prevents prefills from duplicating if KV warm state already in same rack. link: https://git.redwood/pr/flake/1287
maria: ops will retain the billing charge for now, but please add a postmortem note describing the feature-flag gap and the cost guardrail we should bake into routing policy.
aj: agreed. small follow-ups: 1) add egress leash to default dedicated pool templates (toggle=false for non-prod), 2) add metrics alert for per-tenant sustained egress > 60MB/s, 3) review migration steps for tenants promoted to fractional-dedicated. i'll make a checklist.
linus: thanks. one more ask — can we add a cheap probe in the scheduler that simulates a prefill and checks TOR headroom before allowing cross-rack warmups? if cheap, should prevent this class of regression.
priya: good idea. i'll sketch a design doc after breakfast.
oncall-sre: closing loop for now. if anyone sees reappearance ping here. :thumbsup:
